statement: Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms always output the same minimum spanning tree on a given connected weighted graph.
definitions: Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms are taken in their standard textbook form, which does NOT specify how ties between equal-weight edges are broken (nor Prim's start vertex). The claim asserts that every legal run of Kruskal and every legal run of Prim on the same connected weighted graph output the same edge set. A counterexample exhibits a graph, a legal Kruskal run, and a legal Prim run (start vertex and tie-breaks stated) whose outputs are different edge sets; both outputs must be minimum spanning trees.
